### 1928 - Heidegger, Metaphysische Anfangsgründe der Logik im Ausgang von Leibniz (GA 26): A Commentary

`heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary`

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/002` · *Urtranszendenz*
  The source of the idea of being is the primal transcendence of Dasein: understanding of being belongs to the subject only insofar as it is transcending.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-b-interim-reflection-on-the-guiding-thread-of-the-interpretation-of-being` · GA 26 § 5b · [b) Interim Reflection on the Guiding Thread of the Interpretation of Being](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-interim-reflection-on-the-guiding-thread-of-the-interpretation-of-being)
  > We ourselves are the source of the idea of being, but this source must be understood as the "primal transcendence" (*Urtranszendenz*) of Dasein. That is what it means to draw the idea of being from the "subject": understanding of being belongs to the subject only insofar as it is transcending.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/003` · *epekeina tēs ousias*
  Among six determinations of Plato's idea of the good, the sixth is that it is still beyond being, which the commentary reads as 'beyond' in the sense of transcending.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h3-second-main-part-the-metaphysics-of-the-principle-of-reason-as-the-basic-problem` · GA 26, Second Main Part, introduction · [Second Main Part: The Metaphysics of the Principle of Reason as the Basic Problem of Logic](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#second-main-part-the-metaphysics-of-the-principle-of-reason-as-the-basic-problem-of-logic)
  > Heidegger reads the good as the Greek name for what makes being, truth, and order possible, and as "beyond" in the sense of transcending.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/004` · *ontic transcendence*
  Intentionality is an ontically transcending comportment related to beings themselves, but it does not originally constitute this relation, which is founded in being-with beings and ultimately in existence.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-intentionality-and-transcendence` · GA 26 § 9b · [b) Intentionality and Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > It is related to beings themselves and in this sense is an ontically transcending comportment, but it does not originally constitute this relation-to, which is founded in being-with beings.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ga26/005` · *intentionality*
  The previous concept of intentionality is only an ontic transcendence, restricted in scope and conceived theoretically as noesis.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-intentionality-and-transcendence` · GA 26 § 9b · [b) Intentionality and Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > Heidegger fixes three points about the previous concept of intentionality: it is only an ontic transcendence; it concerns existing comportment toward beings only in a certain restriction; and it comes into view only in a narrowing theoretical conception, as *noēsis*.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/006` · *transcendence (vulgar concept)*
  Underlying the subject-object problem is, undiscussed, the problem of transcendence, taken first in its vulgar sense: Dasein passing over to another being, which is thereby disclosed to it.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-intentionality-and-transcendence` · GA 26 § 9b · [b) Intentionality and Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > Underlying the whole problem of the "relation" of "subject" to "object" is, undiscussed, the problem of transcendence, the term first taken quite vulgarly: a being (Dasein) passes over to another being (Dasein or something present at hand)

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/007` · *original transcendence*
  The original phenomenon of transcendence is not identical with the subject-object relation, is more original in scope and kind, and is immediately connected with the problem of being.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-intentionality-and-transcendence` · GA 26 § 9b · [b) Intentionality and Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > For a radical posing of the problem, it is essential to lay free the original phenomenon of transcendence. This problem is not identical with that of the subject–object relation but is more original in scope and kind, and it is immediately connected with the problem of being as such

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ga26/008` · *primal transcendence*
  Intentionality as ontic transcendence is possible only on the basis of original transcendence, being-in-the-world, which makes every intentional relation to beings possible.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-intentionality-and-transcendence` · GA 26 § 9b, p. 170 · [b) Intentionality and Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > Intentionality, as ontic transcendence, is itself possible only on the basis of original transcendence, being-in-the-world. This primal transcendence makes possible every intentional relation to beings.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/009` · *transcendence*
  Original transcendence and the understanding of being stand in an inner kinship and in the end are one and the same.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-intentionality-and-transcendence` · GA 26 § 9b, p. 170 · [b) Intentionality and Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > then there must be an inner kinship between original transcendence and understanding of being as such; "indeed, in the end they are one and the same."

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/010` · *transcendence*
  Because being-true as being-disclosive belongs to being-with what is present at hand, the essence of truth as a whole can be clarified only as the problem of transcendence.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-intentionality-and-transcendence` · GA 26 § 9b · [b) Intentionality and Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > The essence of truth as a whole can therefore be clarified only as the problem of transcendence as such.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/011` · *transcendence*
  The basic aim of the analytic of Dasein is to exhibit the inner possibility of the understanding of being, which is at the same time the inner possibility of transcendence.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s10-the-problem-of-transcendence-and-the-problem-of-being-and-time` · GA 26 § 10 · [§10. The Problem of Transcendence and the Problem of Being and Time](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#the-problem-of-transcendence-and-the-problem-of-being-and-time)
  > Its basic aim is to exhibit the inner possibility of the understanding of being, which means at the same time the inner possibility of transcendence.

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ga26/012` · *transcendence*
  The problem of transcendence must be posed as universally and radically as the problem of being, not restricted to the subject's relation to independent things or to a region of beings.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s10-the-problem-of-transcendence-and-the-problem-of-being-and-time` · GA 26 § 10 · [§10. The Problem of Transcendence and the Problem of Being and Time](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#the-problem-of-transcendence-and-the-problem-of-being-and-time)
  > The problem of transcendence must be posed as universally and radically as the problem of being. It is not a problem restricted to the relation of the subject to the things independent of it, nor a question about a particular region of beings.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/013` · *transcendence*
  In the second of three theses, transcendence lies in the essence of existence as the giving of world before all being toward intraworldly beings.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s10-the-problem-of-transcendence-and-the-problem-of-being-and-time` · GA 26 § 10 · [§10. The Problem of Transcendence and the Problem of Being and Time](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#the-problem-of-transcendence-and-the-problem-of-being-and-time)
  > Transcendence lies in the essence of existence, that is, the giving of world before all being toward and with intraworldly beings.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/014` · *transcendere*
  From transcendere, transcendence means passing over or surpassing; the verbal sense includes an action, a relation from something to something, and something passed over.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > The word comes from *transcendere*: to climb over, step over, pass over to. Transcendence therefore means the passing over, the surpassing; the transcendent designates that to which the passage is made

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/015` · *the transcendent*
  The philosophical term has two main meanings: the transcendent as opposed to the immanent, and the transcendent as opposed to the contingent.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > the term means the transcendent in distinction from the immanent, and the transcendent in distinction from the contingent.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ga26/016` · *immanence*
  Wherever transcendence is posed against the counterconcept of immanence, the capsule representation of the subject underlies it in principle.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > But however and wherever the problem of transcendence is posed, in explicit or implicit orientation on the counterconcept of immanence, the capsule representation of the subject, of Dasein, underlies it in principle.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ga26/017` · *epistemological concept of transcendence*
  Transcendence with immanence as counterconcept first makes epistemology possible, and if that concept falls, epistemology as such falls with it.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > This concept of transcendence, with immanence as its counterconcept, first makes possible what is called epistemology, so Heidegger calls it the epistemological concept of transcendence.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/018` · *theological concept of transcendence*
  The transcendent as opposed to the contingent means the unconditioned and inaccessible, predominantly the divine, which yields a theological concept of transcendence.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > Insofar as the transcendent in this second concept always somehow means the unconditioned, the absolute, and this is predominantly called the divine, one can speak of a theological concept of transcendence.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ga26/019` · *the transcendent*
  The epistemological and theological concepts are coupled, so that the problem of the external world becomes entwined with the knowledge of God and the proof of his existence.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > The question of the possible grasping of the transcendent in the epistemological sense becomes entwined with the question of the possibility of knowing the transcendent object in the theological sense.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/020` · *finite ecstatic transcendence*
  Kant's 'outside us' means either what we are not, accessible within the ecstatic transcendence of thrown Dasein, or what lies outside any access by finite ecstatic transcendence, appearances considered in themselves.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a, A 373 · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > But "outside us" can also mean what we not only are not, but what lies outside accessibility by finite ecstatic transcendence, namely appearances insofar as they are considered in themselves.

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ga26/021` · *transcendence*
  Kant's Critique as a whole circles around the problem of transcendence, which in the original sense is not epistemological but the problem of freedom.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a, p. 210 · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > Kant's *Critique of Pure Reason* as a whole circles around the problem of transcendence, "which in the original sense is precisely not an epistemological problem but the problem of freedom" (p. 210)

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ga26/022` · *transcendence*
  Against both concepts, transcendence is neither a relation between inner and outer spheres, nor primarily the knowing relation of subject to object, nor the title for what is inaccessible to finite knowledge.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > transcendence is neither a relation between an inner and an outer sphere, such that what is surpassed in it would be a barrier belonging to the subject that separated it from the outer sphere, nor primarily the knowing relation of a subject to an object

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ga26/023` · *transcendence*
  Transcendence is the original constitution of the subjectivity of a subject: to be a subject means to transcend, and Dasein itself is the passage.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a, p. 211 · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > "To be a subject means to transcend" (p. 211). Dasein does not exist and then occasionally carry out a passage; existing means originally surpassing. "Dasein itself is the passage."

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/024` · *transcendence*
  A note holds that the understanding of being as the overpowering, as holiness, must be clarified from Dasein's transcendence rather than by proving the divine ontically.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a, note · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > the problem of transcendence must be taken back into the question of temporality and freedom, and only from there can it be shown how far the understanding of being as the overpowering, as holiness, belongs to transcendence itself

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/025` · *what is surpassed*
  Transcendence is not crossing a barrier around an inner space; what is surpassed is beings themselves, which can become manifest precisely on the basis of transcendence.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > Second, transcendence does not mean the crossing of a barrier that first shut the subject into an inner space. What is surpassed is beings themselves, which can become manifest to the subject precisely on the basis of its transcendence.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/026` · *transcending*
  As transcending, Dasein is beyond nature though as factical it remains embraced by it, and as transcending, that is as free, it is alien to nature.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a, p. 212 · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > In other words, as transcending, Dasein is beyond nature, although as factical it remains embraced by it. "As transcending, that is, as free, Dasein is something alien to nature" (p. 212).

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/027` · *world*
  What the subject transcends toward is not an object or any being but world.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a, p. 212 · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > "What the subject transcends toward is what we call world" (p. 212).

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/028` · *being-in-the-world*
  Because transcendence is Dasein's basic constitution and surpasses toward a world, the basic phenomenon of Dasein's transcendence is called being-in-the-world.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > the basic phenomenon of Dasein's transcendence is called being-in-the-world.

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ga26/029` · *transcendence*
  Even saying that Dasein is always already outside with beings is skewed, since it presupposes that Dasein was once inside.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > Insofar as Dasein, as being-in-the-world, exists, it is always already outside with beings; indeed this way of speaking is still skewed, since "already outside" presupposes that it was once inside.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/030` · *transcendence*
  In Being and Time the analyses of anxiety, worldhood, conscience and death serve the progressive working out of transcendence until it becomes explicitly a problem in § 69.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > until it becomes a problem again explicitly in §69: "The Temporality of Being-in-the-World and the Problem of the Transcendence of the World." Transcendence is still, indeed only now, a problem there.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ga26/031` · *transcendence*
  Transcendence, being-in-the-world, is nowhere identified with intentionality, and whoever does so shows how far they are from understanding the phenomenon.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > Transcendence, being-in-the-world, is nowhere equated or identified with intentionality; whoever does so, as repeatedly happens, only shows how far they are from understanding the phenomenon

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/032` · *transcendence*
  The thesis of transcendence is an essential statement about what Dasein is, not a factual statement that it exists.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence` · GA 26 § 11a, p. 217 · [a) On the Concept of Transcendence](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#a-on-the-concept-of-transcendence)
  > The statement of transcendence about existence is "an existential (ontological) statement, not an existentiell (ontic) one" (p. 217).

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/033` · *world*
  Because world belongs to transcendence as such, it is a transcendental concept in the strict sense, here equivalent to fundamental-ontological.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-the-phenomenon-of-world` · GA 26 § 11b · [b) The Phenomenon of World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-the-phenomenon-of-world)
  > Because world belongs to transcendence as such, it is a transcendental concept in the strict sense.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/034` · *transcendental concept of world*
  Of four concepts of world, the fourth is ontological and means the metaphysical essence of Dasein with regard to its basic constitution, transcendence.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-the-phenomenon-of-world` · GA 26 § 11b · [b) The Phenomenon of World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-the-phenomenon-of-world)
  > fourth, an ontological concept of world that does not mean human society ontically but ontologically the metaphysical essence of Dasein as such, with regard to its basic metaphysical constitution: transcendence.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/035` · *self-transcendence*
  In transcendence Dasein leaps over itself as a being, and this leap-over makes selfhood possible and opens the abyss Dasein is for itself.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-the-phenomenon-of-world` · GA 26 § 11b · [b) The Phenomenon of World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-the-phenomenon-of-world)
  > in transcendence Dasein leaps over precisely itself as a being, more precisely, this leap-over makes it possible for Dasein to be something like itself.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ga26/036` · *transcendence*
  The doctrine of ideas, motivated by transcendence, could not reach world because it took the relation to the ideas as an intensified intuition of beings.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-the-phenomenon-of-world` · GA 26 § 11b · [b) The Phenomenon of World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-the-phenomenon-of-world)
  > the doctrine of ideas could not reach the concept of world, because the ideas and the comportment toward them counted only as an intensification of a certain grasping of beings, namely intuition.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ga26/037` · *transcendence*
  Transcendence cannot be housed in theoretical, aesthetic or practical comportment; it lies before every mode of comportment, before noesis and before orexis.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-the-phenomenon-of-world` · GA 26 § 11b · [b) The Phenomenon of World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-the-phenomenon-of-world)
  > Transcendence lies before every possible mode of comportment, before *noēsis*, but also before *orexis*.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/038` · *epekeina tēs ousias*
  In Plato the idea of the good lies beyond the ideas, and since the ideas are already transcendent relative to changing beings, this transcendence must be the most original.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-the-phenomenon-of-world` · GA 26 § 11b · [b) The Phenomenon of World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-the-phenomenon-of-world)
  > Here a transcendence appears which, since the ideas are already transcendent relative to changing beings, must be claimed as the most original.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/039` · *for-the-sake-of*
  The idea of the good is read as the for-the-sake-of, and the for-the-sake-of is the basic character of world that gives its wholeness transcendental organization.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-the-phenomenon-of-world` · GA 26 § 11b, p. 238 · [b) The Phenomenon of World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-the-phenomenon-of-world)
  > "the basic character of world, by which the wholeness receives its specifically transcendental form of organization, is the for-the-sake-of" (p. 238).

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/040` · *transcendence*
  Since a for-the-sake-of is possible only where there is a will, the transcendence of Dasein and freedom are identical.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-b-the-phenomenon-of-world` · GA 26 § 11b, p. 238 · [b) The Phenomenon of World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#b-the-phenomenon-of-world)
  > "Only where there is freedom is there a for-the-sake-of, and only there is there world. In short: the transcendence of Dasein and freedom are identical!" (p. 238).

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/041` · *transcending*
  In transcending, Dasein transcends every being, itself, co-Dasein and beings not of its character, so that choosing itself is choosing its being-with others and with things.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-c-freedom-and-world` · GA 26 § 11c · [c) Freedom and World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#c-freedom-and-world)
  > In transcending, Dasein transcends every being: itself, every being of its kind (co-Dasein), and beings not of Dasein's character.

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ga26/042` · *transcendence*
  Spontaneity's 'of itself' is undetermined without selfhood, so transcendence must be taken back into freedom and its basic essence sought in freedom itself.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-c-freedom-and-world` · GA 26 § 11c · [c) Freedom and World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#c-freedom-and-world)
  > But this "of itself" remains undetermined without selfhood, which means one must take transcendence back into freedom, indeed seek the basic essence of transcendence in freedom itself.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/043` · *Widerhalt*
  World is the free counter-hold of Dasein's for-the-sake-of, and being-in-the-world is therefore nothing other than freedom.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-c-freedom-and-world` · GA 26 § 11c, p. 248 · [c) Freedom and World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#c-freedom-and-world)
  > "World is the free counter-hold (*Widerhalt*) of the for-the-sake-of of Dasein" (p. 248). Being-in-the-world is therefore nothing other than freedom

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/044` · *transcending*
  World, as the whole of Dasein's inner possibilities as transcending, surpasses everything actual, so that actual beings show themselves as a restriction of an excess of possibilities.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-c-freedom-and-world` · GA 26 § 11c · [c) Freedom and World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#c-freedom-and-world)
  > World, as the whole of the essential inner possibilities of Dasein as transcending, surpasses everything actual.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/045` · *transcendence*
  Despair, as complete factical unfreedom, is an elementary testimony to transcendence because the despairing person sees the impossibility of the possible.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-c-freedom-and-world` · GA 26 § 11c · [c) Freedom and World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#c-freedom-and-world)
  > Even this complete factical unfreedom is an elementary testimony to transcendence, for despair consists precisely in the despairing person's seeing the impossibility of the possible.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/046` · *Überschwung*
  The surpassing of the factically existent that lies in world, transcendence and freedom corresponds to the epekeina, and Dasein is distinguished by a swinging over.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-c-freedom-and-world` · GA 26 § 11c · [c) Freedom and World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#c-freedom-and-world)
  > World itself is surpassing (*übertrifftig*); a being of Dasein's character is distinguished by a "swinging over" (*Überschwung*); world is the free, surpassing counter-hold of the for-the-sake-of.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/047` · *world-entry*
  Seen from being-in-the-world, factically existing Dasein is the existing possibility of the world-entry of beings.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-c-freedom-and-world` · GA 26 § 11c, p. 249 · [c) Freedom and World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#c-freedom-and-world)
  > Seen metaphysically from being-in-the-world, Dasein as factically existing is nothing other than "the existing possibility of the world-entry of beings" (p. 249).

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/048` · *world-entry*
  World-entry is not a process in present things but something that happens with them when transcendence happens, that is, when historical Dasein exists.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-c-freedom-and-world` · GA 26 § 11c · [c) Freedom and World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#c-freedom-and-world)
  > World-entry happens when transcendence happens, that is, when historical Dasein exists; only then is a being-in-the-world of Dasein existent.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/049` · *world-entry*
  World-entry is the presupposition not for a present thing's being present but for its manifesting itself as not needing world-entry for its own being.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-c-freedom-and-world` · GA 26 § 11c · [c) Freedom and World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#c-freedom-and-world)
  > World-entry and its happening are the presupposition not for the present thing first becoming present and coming into what reveals itself to us as its presence, but only for its manifesting itself precisely in its not needing world-entry for its own being.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/050` · *transcendence*
  The inner possibility of transcendence, being-in-the-world as swinging-over toward the counter-hold, is time as original temporality.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h6-c-freedom-and-world` · GA 26 § 11c, p. 252 · [c) Freedom and World](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#c-freedom-and-world)
  > "The inner possibility of transcendence, I assert, is time as original temporality!" (p. 252).

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ga26/051` · *transcendence*
  Freedom itself transcends, and intentional relation is only the factical way of appropriating what has already been leapt over and disclosed on the basis of transcendence.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s12-transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium` · GA 26 § 12 · [§12. Transcendence and Temporality (nihil originarium)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium)
  > the intentional relation is only the particular factical way of appropriating what has already been leapt over, that is, disclosed, on the basis of transcendence.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/052` · *transcendence*
  The then is found neither in objects nor in subjects but 'underway from subject to object', which is the passage, transcendence.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s12-transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium` · GA 26 § 12 · [§12. Transcendence and Temporality (nihil originarium)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium)
  > Neither in objects nor in subjects (in the traditional sense), neither here nor there, but, as it were, "underway from subject to object!" We already know this underway: as the passage, transcendence.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/053` · *Entrückung*
  Awaiting is the rapture into the then-like that underlies hope, fear and expectation, having leapt ahead beyond all possible beings.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s12-transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium` · GA 26 § 12 · [§12. Transcendence and Temporality (nihil originarium)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium)
  > What was called awaiting is nothing other than the "rapture" (*Entrückung*) into the then-like that underlies those comportments, which has already leapt ahead beyond all possible beings of which we can and must say they are "then."

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/054` · *transcendence*
  The ecstematic unity of the horizon of temporality is the temporal condition of the possibility of world, and transcendence has its possibility in the unity of ecstatic oscillation.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s12-transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium` · GA 26 § 12 · [§12. Transcendence and Temporality (nihil originarium)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium)
  > This ecstematic unity of the horizon of temporality is nothing other than the temporal condition of the possibility of world and its essential belonging to transcendence. Transcendence has its possibility in the unity of ecstatic oscillation.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ga26/055` · *transcendence*
  Against Leibniz, monads have no windows not because they contain everything but because there is no inside or outside, temporalizing being the ecstatic happening of world-entry.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s12-transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium` · GA 26 § 12, p. 271 · [§12. Transcendence and Temporality (nihil originarium)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium)
  > "We would say, conversely: they have no windows, not because they have everything inside, but because there is neither an inside nor an outside, because temporalizing (the drive) means in itself the ecstatic happening of world-entry

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/056` · *transcendence*
  The origin of transcendence is temporality itself, so that with temporalizing, transcendence and world-entry already happen.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s12-transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium` · GA 26 § 12 · [§12. Transcendence and Temporality (nihil originarium)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium)
  > The origin (*origo*) of transcendence is temporality itself, such that with temporalizing, transcendence, and that is, world-entry, already happens.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/057` · *swinging-over*
  Heraclitus' self-increasing logos is read as Dasein enriching itself, with the character of being-richer-than, of swinging-over.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s12-transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium` · GA 26 § 12 · [§12. Transcendence and Temporality (nihil originarium)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#transcendence-and-temporality-nihil-originarium)
  > The original inner possibility of enrichment lies essentially in Dasein; it always has the character of being-richer-than, of swinging-over.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga26/058` · *transcendence*
  The surpassing of beings in all dimensions in transcendence is grounded in the ecstatic constitution of temporality, whose horizon is temporalized primarily from the future, the for-the-sake-of.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s13-transcendence-temporalizing-itself-in-temporality-and-the-essence-of-ground` · GA 26 § 13 · [§13. Transcendence Temporalizing Itself in Temporality and the Essence of Ground](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#transcendence-temporalizing-itself-in-temporality-and-the-essence-of-ground)
  > The surpassing of beings in all dimensions in transcendence is grounded in the ecstatic constitution of temporality.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/059` · *for-the-sake-of*
  We ask why because transcendence temporalizes itself, and the for-the-sake-of, as the primary character of world and of transcendence, is the primal phenomenon of ground.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s13-transcendence-temporalizing-itself-in-temporality-and-the-essence-of-ground` · GA 26 § 13, p. 276 · [§13. Transcendence Temporalizing Itself in Temporality and the Essence of Ground](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#transcendence-temporalizing-itself-in-temporality-and-the-essence-of-ground)
  > "The for-the-sake-of, as the primary character of world, that is, of transcendence, is the primal phenomenon of ground as such" (p. 276).

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/060` · *transcendental freedom*
  The metaphysical essence of transcendingly existing Dasein is freedom, and transcendental freedom is freedom toward ground.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s13-transcendence-temporalizing-itself-in-temporality-and-the-essence-of-ground` · GA 26 § 13, p. 276 · [§13. Transcendence Temporalizing Itself in Temporality and the Essence of Ground](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#transcendence-temporalizing-itself-in-temporality-and-the-essence-of-ground)
  > "We can say quite lapidarily: the metaphysical essence of Dasein existing transcendingly is freedom. But freedom, as transcendental freedom, is freedom toward ground" (p. 276).

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ga26/061` · *swinging-over*
  On the basis of its swinging-over Dasein is above beings, but precisely so that it experiences beings in resistance as that against which it is powerless.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s13-transcendence-temporalizing-itself-in-temporality-and-the-essence-of-ground` · GA 26 § 13, p. 279 · [§13. Transcendence Temporalizing Itself in Temporality and the Essence of Ground](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#transcendence-temporalizing-itself-in-temporality-and-the-essence-of-ground)
  > On the basis of this swinging-over, Dasein is always above beings, as we say, but precisely so that it first experiences beings in resistance as that against which transcending Dasein is powerless.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga26/062` · *veritas transcendentalis*
  The disclosing that lies in the ecstatic unity of temporality is original being-true, the truth that transcendence itself is, and the condition of every ontic-intentional truth.
  `heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary#h5-s14-the-essence-of-ground-and-the-idea-of-logic` · GA 26 § 14 · [§14. The Essence of Ground and the Idea of Logic](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-26-metaphysische-anfangsgruende-der-logik-commentary.html#the-essence-of-ground-and-the-idea-of-logic)
  > This disclosing is metaphysically original being-true, the truth that transcendence itself is: *veritas transcendentalis*.

`heidegger-ga-3-kant-und-das-problem-der-metaphysik-commentary`

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga3/002` · *Überschritt*
  Metaphysics performs a crossing-over beyond what experience offers toward the supersensible, and the commentary notes that this word will become transcendence, the book's whole subject.
  `heidegger-ga-3-kant-und-das-problem-der-metaphysik-commentary#h3-s-2-the-starting-point-of-the-laying-of-the-ground-of-traditional-metaphysics` · GA 3 § 2, B xv · [§ 2.   > The crossing-over is registered as a fact about metaphysics before it is analysed; that word, *Überschritt*, will shortly become *Transzendenz*, and the whole book is the analysis of it.

  > It concerns the crossing-over (transcendence) of pure reason to beings, such that experience can now first conform to them as possible objects. ### 1929 to 1949 - Heidegger, GA 9 — Vom Wesen des Grundes

`heidegger-ga-9-vom-wesen-des-grundes-commentary`

#### Vom Wesen des Grundes, 1929

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga9/002` · *transcendence*
  The domain within which the essence of ground can be treated is transcendence, and the problem of ground in turn determines transcendence more originally.
  `heidegger-ga-9-vom-wesen-des-grundes-commentary#h2-on-the-essence-of-ground` · GA 9: 124-126 · [On the Essence of Ground](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-9-vom-wesen-des-grundes-commentary.html#on-the-essence-of-ground)
  > That domain is transcendence, and the relation runs both ways: the problem of ground in turn determines transcendence more originally.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ga9/003` · *transcendence of Dasein*
  The capacity to distinguish being from beings must be rooted in the ground of Dasein's essence, and Heidegger provisionally names this ground of the ontological difference the transcendence of Dasein.
  `heidegger-ga-9-vom-wesen-des-grundes-commentary#h3-i-the-problem-of-ground` · GA 9: 133-135 · [I. The Problem of Ground](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-9-vom-wesen-des-grundes-commentary.html#i-the-problem-of-ground)
  > Heidegger names this ground of the difference, provisionally, the transcendence of Dasein.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga9/004` · *transcendence*
  Intentionality, as the name for all comportment toward beings, is possible only on the ground of transcendence and is neither identical with it nor what makes it possible.
  `heidegger-ga-9-vom-wesen-des-grundes-commentary#h3-i-the-problem-of-ground` · GA 9: 135 · [I. The Problem of Ground](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-9-vom-wesen-des-grundes-commentary.html#i-the-problem-of-ground)
  > If all comportment toward beings is called intentional, intentionality is possible only on the ground of transcendence; it is neither identical with transcendence nor what makes transcendence possible.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ga9/005` · *transcendence*
  Because the essence of ground relates internally to the essence of truth, the question of the essence of ground becomes the problem of transcendence.
  `heidegger-ga-9-vom-wesen-des-grundes-commentary#h3-i-the-problem-of-ground` · GA 9: 135 · [I. The Problem of Ground](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/heidegger/heidegger-ga-9-vom-wesen-des-grundes-commentary.html#i-the-problem-of-ground)
  > The question of the essence of ground becomes the problem of transcendence.

  `husserliana-1-cartesianische-meditationen-commentary#h3-s-11-the-psychological-and-the-transcendental-ego-the-transcendence-of-the-world` · CM § 11 · [§ 11. ### 1935 - Krisis Commentary

`husserl-krisis-commentary`

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/krisis/001` · *psychological immanence*
  The Meditations substituted the psychic I for the ego and psychological immanence for egological immanence, with historical effect to the present.
  `husserl-krisis-commentary#h3-s-19-descartes-overriding-interest-in-objectivism-as-the-ground-of-his-self-misi` · Krisis § 19 · [§ 19 Descartes' overriding interest in objectivism as the ground of his self-misinterpretation](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserl-krisis-commentary.html#descartes-overriding-interest-in-objectivism-as-the-ground-of-his-self-misinterpretation)
  > The Meditations worked themselves out in the fateful form of a substitution of the ego's own psychic I for the ego, psychological immanence for egological immanence

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/krisis/002` · *cognition transcending the ego*
  Descartes' founding of philosophy from the ego is an epistemology of how the ego brings about objective cognition, which for him means cognition transcending the ego metaphysically.
  `husserl-krisis-commentary#h3-s-20-intentionality-in-descartes` · Krisis § 20 · [§ 20 "Intentionality" in Descartes](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserl-krisis-commentary.html#intentionality-in-descartes)
  > a theory of how the ego in the intentionality of its reason brings about objective cognition, which for Descartes means: cognition transcending the ego metaphysically

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/krisis/003` · *transcendent "in-itself"*
  Rationalism held that the method more geometrico can cognize the world thought of as a transcendent in-itself, and English empiricism reacted against this reach into a transcendent.
  `husserl-krisis-commentary#h3-s-21-descartes-as-point-of-departure-for-the-two-lines-of-development-rationalis` · Krisis § 21 · [§ 21 Descartes as point of departure for the two lines of development: rationalism and empiricism](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserl-krisis-commentary.html#descartes-as-point-of-departure-for-the-two-lines-of-development-rationalism-and-empiricism)
  > Against this conviction — against such a reach of the new science into a "transcendent" — reacts English empiricism, though itself also strongly determined by Descartes.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/krisis/004` · *immanence*
  Cartesian presuppositionlessness demanded subjectively directed considerations, the return to the cognizing I in its immanence.
  `husserl-krisis-commentary#h3-s-24-the-genuine-philosophical-motive-of-the-shattering-of-objectivism-hidden-in` · Krisis § 24 · [§ 24 The genuine philosophical motive of the shattering of objectivism, hidden in the countersense of Humean skepticism](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserl-krisis-commentary.html#the-genuine-philosophical-motive-of-the-shattering-of-objectivism-hidden-in-the-countersense-of-humean-skepticism)
  > The Cartesian radicalism of presuppositionlessness demanded subjectively directed considerations, the return to the cognizing I in its immanence.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/krisis/005` · *transcendent affection*
  For Kant the natural-scientific world is a formation of the intellect, with the proviso that sensory material stems from a transcendent affection by things in themselves.
  `husserl-krisis-commentary#h3-s-25-the-transcendental-motive-in-rationalism-kant-s-conception-of-a-transcenden` · Krisis § 25 · [§ 25 The "transcendental" motive in rationalism: Kant's conception of a transcendental philosophy](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserl-krisis-commentary.html#the-transcendental-motive-in-rationalism-kants-conception-of-a-transcendental-philosophy)

  > This auto-affection, transcendence's being-already-affected before it affects itself as time, conditions all ontological affection by the world and all affection by beings, and conditions inner sense.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/em/071` · *transcendence*

  > Feeling's surpassing thus takes place within its immanence, the surpassing of the feeling toward what it feels — yet in surpassing itself this way, the feeling surpasses itself toward nothing, does not surpass itself at all: it is feeling's being-seized by its own reality.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/em/073` · *transcendence*

### 1965 - Philosophie et phénoménologie du corps — Commentary

`henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary`

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ppc/002` · *transcendent being*
  The premise the whole Introduction attacks is that the body is transcendent being, a denizen of the world where subjectivity does not reside.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h2-introduction-the-apparent-contingency-of-the-question-concerning-the-body-and-th` · PPC, Introduction · [Introduction. The Apparent Contingency of the Question Concerning the Body and the Necessity of an Ontological Analysis of the Body](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#introduction-the-apparent-contingency-of-the-question-concerning-the-body-and-the-necessity-of-an-ontological-analysis-of-the-body)
  > The stakes are set by a single premise the whole Introduction will attack: that the body is transcendent being, a denizen of the world where subjectivity does not reside.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ppc/003` · *transcendent being*
  Whatever region the body is assigned to, biological, living or specifically human, the problem remains contingent, since every such region is a structure of transcendent being in general.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h2-introduction-the-apparent-contingency-of-the-question-concerning-the-body-and-th` · PPC, Introduction · [Introduction. The Apparent Contingency of the Question Concerning the Body and the Necessity of an Ontological Analysis of the Body](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#introduction-the-apparent-contingency-of-the-question-concerning-the-body-and-the-necessity-of-an-ontological-analysis-of-the-body)
  > Whatever region we finally assign our body to, biological, living, or a *sui generis* human region, in every case we deal only with specifications and structures of transcendent being in general, however great the differences between them.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ppc/004` · *transcendent being*
  For Biran being given through a phenomenological distance is transcendent being, known by exterior knowledge, while being given without distance is the self, known by 'reflection'.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h3-s-1-the-phenomenological-presuppositions-of-biranian-ontology` · PPC, ch. I § 1 · [§ 1. The Phenomenological Presuppositions of Biranian Ontology](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#the-phenomenological-presuppositions-of-biranian-ontology)
  > In the first, being is given through the mediation of a phenomenological distance; this is transcendent being, and Biran calls the corresponding knowledge exterior knowledge.

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ppc/005` · *transcendence*
  Biranian 'reflection' names the self-knowledge included in every intentionality, which does not go toward the world, so it is opposed to the movement of transcendence rather than a case of it.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h3-s-1-the-phenomenological-presuppositions-of-biranian-ontology` · PPC, ch. I § 1 · [§ 1. The Phenomenological Presuppositions of Biranian Ontology](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#the-phenomenological-presuppositions-of-biranian-ontology)
  > Reflection is thus opposed to the movement of transcendence and cannot designate a particular case of it, namely classical reflection.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ppc/006` · *transcendental inner experience*
  Conscious life is not given in a transcendent inner experience such as introspection but in a transcendental inner experience, the revelation of lived experience to itself in immanence.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h3-s-1-the-phenomenological-presuppositions-of-biranian-ontology` · PPC, ch. I § 1 · [§ 1. The Phenomenological Presuppositions of Biranian Ontology](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#the-phenomenological-presuppositions-of-biranian-ontology)
  > Conscious life cannot be given in a transcendent inner experience; it remains that it is given in a *transcendental* inner experience.

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ppc/007` · *transcendence*
  'Transcendental' had to be given a radically immanent signification, so that the a priori conditions of experience would no longer float in the transcendence of a quasi-Platonic heaven.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h3-s-2-the-transcendental-deduction-of-the-categories` · PPC, ch. I § 2 · [§ 2. The Transcendental Deduction of the Categories](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#the-transcendental-deduction-of-the-categories)
  > What was needed was to give "transcendental" a radically immanent signification, so that the ensemble of *a priori* conditions of the possibility of experience would no longer float in an indeterminate region and in the transcendence of a quasi-Platonic heaven.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ppc/008` · *transcendent term*
  Biran's critique of the a priori is that it cannot be a posited transcendent term = x but must belong to the sphere of absolute immanence and coincide with the being of intentionality.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h3-s-2-the-transcendental-deduction-of-the-categories` · PPC, ch. I § 2 · [§ 2. The Transcendental Deduction of the Categories](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#the-transcendental-deduction-of-the-categories)
  > Biran's critique amounts to saying that the *a priori* cannot be a transcendent term, known or unknown, situated before or behind us, but belongs to the sphere of absolute immanence.

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ppc/009` · *transcendent*
  Before its deduction a category appears as a character of transcendent being, and its deduction is a reduction in which it passes from the transcendent sphere to that of immanence.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h3-s-2-the-transcendental-deduction-of-the-categories` · PPC, ch. I § 2 · [§ 2. The Transcendental Deduction of the Categories](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#the-transcendental-deduction-of-the-categories)
  > It must be deduced, that is, a reduction must intervene in which its being undergoes a transformation and passes from the sphere of the transcendent to that of immanence and subjectivity.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ppc/010` · *transcendent being*
  Empiricism's reduction is true on the plane of transcendent being, where there is no room for causality; its error is confining the inquiry to that plane.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h3-s-2-the-transcendental-deduction-of-the-categories` · PPC, ch. I § 2 · [§ 2.   > The phenomenological reduction performed by empiricism and positivism is true on its own plane, that of transcendent being: it shows that on such a plane there is no room for the idea of causality

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/ppc/011` · *transcendent being*
  The deduction of substance reveals in Biranism a kind of ontological proof: the resisting continuum is an element of absolute certainty at the heart of transcendent being.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h3-s-2-the-transcendental-deduction-of-the-categories` · PPC, ch. I § 2 · [§ 2.   > The deduction of substance has the merit of bringing to light one of Biranism's riches, the presence within it of a kind of ontological proof revealing an element of absolute certainty at the heart of transcendent being.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ppc/012` · *transcendent being*
  Because the category is identical with the ego's being, the ego cannot be constituted by it and is torn away from transcendent being, which is always the product of constitution.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h3-s-3-the-theory-of-the-ego-and-the-problem-of-the-soul` · PPC, ch. I § 3 · [§ 3. The Theory of the Ego and the Problem of the Soul](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#the-theory-of-the-ego-and-the-problem-of-the-soul)
  > The deduction has the capital consequence of tearing the ego's being away from the sphere of transcendent being in general, which is always the product of a constitution.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ppc/013` · *transcendence of the ego*
  The assertion of a transcendence of the ego is groundless and frivolous because it destroys the interiority of immediate self-presence that constitutes ipseity.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h3-s-3-the-theory-of-the-ego-and-the-problem-of-the-soul` · PPC, ch. I § 3 · [§ 3. The Theory of the Ego and the Problem of the Soul](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#the-theory-of-the-ego-and-the-problem-of-the-soul)
  > The assertion of a transcendence of the ego thereby appears groundless and, since it destroys the character constituting the very essence of ipseity, frivolous.

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ppc/014` · *transcendence*
  The ego's self-manifestation excludes the manifestation of exteriority while founding it, so immanence is not a region alongside transcendence but what makes it possible.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h3-s-3-the-theory-of-the-ego-and-the-problem-of-the-soul` · PPC, ch. I § 3 · [§ 3.   > The relation "excludes while founding" is Henry's formula for the whole architecture: immanence is not one region alongside transcendence but what makes transcendence possible by being categorically unlike it.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ppc/015` · *transcendent being*
  Biran's critique of Descartes is that he passes from the ego as transcendental inner experience to positing the ego, as soul, as an element of transcendent being.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h3-s-3-the-theory-of-the-ego-and-the-problem-of-the-soul` · PPC, ch. I § 3 · [§ 3. The Theory of the Ego and the Problem of the Soul](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#the-theory-of-the-ego-and-the-problem-of-the-soul)
  > It now runs from the being of the ego, originally and correctly interpreted as that of subjectivity and transcendental inner experience, to positing the ego as an element of *transcendent* being.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ppc/016` · *transcendent being*
  Replacing mechanism with a dynamic or structural model of movement changes nothing so long as the body is an element of transcendent being.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ppc/017` · *transcendent*
  The absolute immanence of the body implies rejecting every analysis that presupposes the body to be in its original being something transcendent, a thing and part of the world.

  > This affirms the absolute immanence of the body, and implies rejecting all analyses commanded by the presupposition that the body is in its original being something transcendent

- **revised** · `transzendenz/ppc/018` · *transcendent experience*
  Since all consciousness is consciousness of something, transcendental inner experience is always also a transcendent experience in which the world is announced.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-ii-the-subjective-body` · PPC, ch. II · [Chapter II. The Subjective Body](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#chapter-ii-the-subjective-body)
  > But all consciousness is consciousness of something; transcendental inner experience is always also a transcendent experience.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ppc/019` · *transcendent term*
  The transcendent term met by movement is discovered in the truth of transcendent being only because movement belongs, as real movement, to absolute immanence.

  > If the transcendent term our movement experiences, given without the mediation of any representation, is nevertheless not a mere phenomenological nothing — if it is effectively discovered in the truth of transcendent being — that is for the sole reason that the movement of our body is not an unconscious or physiological process either

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/ppc/020` · *transcendence of movement*

  > Third, intentionality can be said finite insofar as it relates to a *world*. So understood, finitude is an essential qualification belonging to the being of human reality as such. Every intentionality obeys, by reason of its principled transcendence, this concept.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ppc/050` · *transcendence*
  Immanence is more original than transcendence and its ultimate condition of possibility, so the thesis binding finitude to transcendence rests on forgetting auto-affection.
  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h2-conclusion-the-ontological-theory-of-the-body-and-the-problem-of-incarnation-fle` · PPC, Conclusion · [Conclusion. The Ontological Theory of the Body and the Problem of Incarnation: Flesh and Spirit](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#conclusion-the-ontological-theory-of-the-body-and-the-problem-of-incarnation-flesh-and-spirit)
  > *More original than the phenomenon of transcendence, anterior to it, is that of immanence, in which transcendence in fact finds its ultimate condition of possibility.*

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/ppc/051` · *transcendence*

  `henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary#h2-conclusion-the-ontological-theory-of-the-body-and-the-problem-of-incarnation-fle` · PPC, Conclusion · [Conclusion. The Ontological Theory of the Body and the Problem of Incarnation: Flesh and Spirit](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/henry/henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary.html#conclusion-the-ontological-theory-of-the-body-and-the-problem-of-incarnation-flesh-and-spirit)
  > If the act that transcends can discover a world only insofar as it is first and constantly present to itself within its *auto-affection* in immanence, then the thesis binding finitude and transcendence rests on the forgetting of this most original ontological phenomenon.
