### 1994 - Rudolf Bernet, La vie du sujet: Recherches sur l'interprétation de Husserl dans la phénoménologie — Commentary

`bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary`

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/bernet/002` · *transcendence within immanence*
  Merleau-Ponty and Henry press transcendence and immanence respectively until they endanger a subjectivity understood as transcendence within immanence.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h2-foreword` · p. 2 · [Foreword](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#foreword)
  > Merleau-Ponty and Henry, closer to Husserl's implicit aspirations, press transcendence and immanence respectively until they endanger what was most original in a subjectivity understood as "transcendence within immanence".

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/bernet/003` · *transcendence*
  Henry rejects the presupposition that all appearing is intentionality or ecstatic transcendence, and holds that the appearing of transcendence is a derived form grounded in Life's auto-affection.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h2-introduction-the-phenomenological-reduction-and-the-subject-s-double-life` · p. 7 · [Introduction — The Phenomenological Reduction and the Subject's Double Life](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#introduction--the-phenomenological-reduction-and-the-subjects-double-life)
  > Against the presupposition that every givenness is an affection of the subject's immanence by something exceeding it, Henry demands room for the duplicity of appearing and the recognition that the appearing of transcendence is a derived form

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/bernet/004` · *übersteigen*
  In a marginal note to Fink's Sixth Meditation, Husserl says that whoever transcends his natural self and empirical being-human performs a leap into the reduction.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness` · pp. 11-12 · [The Being of the World and the Being of Constituting Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness)
  > As Husserl puts it in a marginal note, whoever tears himself from his fixation on the world, who transcends (*übersteigen*) "his natural self, his [empirical] being-human", performs a "leap" (*Sprung*).

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/bernet/005` · *transcendence*
  In speaking of the transcendence of Dasein's being-in-the-world Heidegger does more than rename Husserlian intentionality: he opens a new interrogation of the phenomenality of the phenomenon.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h3-heidegger` · pp. 21-22 · [Heidegger](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#heidegger)
  > When Heidegger speaks of the "transcendence" characterizing Dasein's "being-in-the-world" he does much more than rename Husserlian intentionality: he inaugurates a new interrogation of the phenomenality of the phenomenon.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/bernet/006` · *transcendence of Dasein*
  For Heidegger the phenomenological investigation of intentionality issues in the discovery of Dasein's transcendence, which proves to be the ontological foundation of intentionality.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-intentional-consciousness` · pp. 52-53 · [The Being of Intentional Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-intentional-consciousness)
  > In sum: the phenomenological investigation of intentionality issues in the discovery of Dasein's transcendence, which in turn proves to be the ontological foundation of intentionality.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/bernet/007` · *immanent and transcendent objects*
  In Heidegger's reconstruction, Husserl's idealism interprets the being of every being by the distinction between immanent and transcendent objects for a present consciousness.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-intentional-consciousness` · pp. 55-56 · [The Being of Intentional Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-intentional-consciousness)
  > Second, it interprets the sense of being of every being in terms of the distinction between immanent and transcendent objects, so that to be is to be either an immanent or a transcendent object for a present consciousness.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/bernet/008` · *transcendent objects*
  On that reading, transcendent objects have a relative, presumptive existence and transcendental consciousness an absolute existence that would survive the annihilation of the world.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-intentional-consciousness` · pp. 55-56 · [The Being of Intentional Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-intentional-consciousness)
  > whence the relative, presumptive existence of transcendent objects and the absolute, necessary existence of a transcendental consciousness that would survive an annihilation of the world without difficulty.

- **revised** · `transzendenz/bernet/009` · *transcendence*
  Heidegger contests that intentionality resides in a sphere of immanence: the subject of intentionality is a being whose being is openness, transcendence.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-intentional-consciousness` · p. 56 · [The Being of Intentional Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-intentional-consciousness)
  > far from constituting a self-enclosed and absolute domain of being, as Husserl would have it, the subject of intentionality is a being whose being is openness, transcendence

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/bernet/010` · *transcendence of Dasein*
  Heidegger's chief reproach is that Husserl did not carry the analysis of intentionality through to its ontological foundation in Dasein's transcendence.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-intentional-consciousness` · p. 57 · [The Being of Intentional Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-intentional-consciousness)
  > Heidegger's chief reproach is that Husserl did not carry his analysis of intentionality through to its ontological foundation in Dasein's transcendence.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/bernet/011` · *transcendence*
  The pre-understanding of world presupposed in intentional discovering shows the being of the intentional as openness and transcendence, whose horizon leads to ecstatic-horizonal temporality.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-intentional-consciousness` · pp. 58-59 · [The Being of Intentional Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-intentional-consciousness)
  > that pre-understanding informs us about the being of the intentional as existential openness and transcendence; and transcendence with its horizon introduces us to the ecstatic-horizonal nature of temporality.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/bernet/012` · *transcendence*
  For Heidegger the understanding of the being of things and of the self are bound together by the intentionality of being-in-the-world, which is more properly called transcendence.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-intentionality-and-transcendence` · pp. 60-61 · [Intentionality and "Transcendence"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > For Heidegger the two ontological questions are necessarily bound together, in virtue of the intentionality of being-in-the-world, which permits at once the understanding of the being of things and the understanding of the being of the self (*Selbst*); and that intentionality of being-in-the-world is more properly called transcendence.

- **revised** · `transzendenz/bernet/013` · *transcendence*
  Understanding any being is a matter of transcendence, a form of intentionality preceding the distinction of subject and object, so Husserlian intentionality, if essentially different, contributes nothing to ontology.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-intentionality-and-transcendence` · p. 61 · [Intentionality and "Transcendence"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > Understanding being, whatever being is in question, is a matter of transcendence, and transcendence is a form of intentionality preceding the distinction between subject and object, interiority and exteriority.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/bernet/014` · *Urtranszendenz*
  Heidegger everywhere treats the relation as founding: intentionality is ontic transcendence grounded in the primal transcendence of being-in-the-world.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-intentionality-and-transcendence` · pp. 61-62 · [Intentionality and "Transcendence"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > everywhere he envisages the relation as one of founding: intentionality is an ontic comportment, an "ontic transcendence", finding its ontological foundation in the primal transcendence (*Urtranszendenz*) of being-in-the-world.

- **revised** · `transzendenz/bernet/015` · *transcendence*
  There is no pure transcendence; intentionality is one of the ways transcendence is ordinarily accomplished, first in ontic comportment and concern.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-intentionality-and-transcendence` · pp. 62-63 · [Intentionality and "Transcendence"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > There is no pure transcendence: intentionality is one of the ways transcendence is ordinarily accomplished.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/bernet/016` · *transcendence*
  Heidegger's formula is that intentionality is the ratio cognoscendi of transcendence and transcendence the ratio essendi of intentionality.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-intentionality-and-transcendence` · pp. 62-63 · [Intentionality and "Transcendence"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > Hence Heidegger's slightly scholastic formula for their mutual relation: intentionality is the *ratio cognoscendi* of transcendence, and transcendence the *ratio essendi* of intentionality in its various modes.

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/bernet/017` · *transcendence*
  The echo of Kant's freedom and moral law is not fortuitous, since transcendence is a freedom that first imposes itself on Dasein as a constraint.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-intentionality-and-transcendence` · pp. 62-63 · [Intentionality and "Transcendence"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > the verbal association is neither wholly fortuitous nor insignificant, since transcendence is a freedom that first imposes itself on Dasein as a constraint

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/bernet/018` · *transcendence*
  For Heidegger the subject is a burst, disseminated unity because Dasein's being-in-the-world is intentionality without reserve, that is, transcendence.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-intentionality-and-transcendence` · pp. 63-64 · [Intentionality and "Transcendence"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > for Heidegger the subject is a burst, disseminated unity (*Streuung*, *Zerstreuung*), since Dasein's being-in-the-world is an intentionality without reserve, that is, transcendence.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/bernet/019` · *intentionality as transcendence*
  Husserl came closest to a conception of intentionality as transcendence in his phenomenology of time and temporalization.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-intentionality-and-transcendence` · pp. 63-64 · [Intentionality and "Transcendence"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#intentionality-and-transcendence)
  > It is doubtless in his phenomenology of time and temporalization that Husserl came closest to a conception of intentionality as transcendence

- **presupposed** · `transzendenz/bernet/020` · *transcends*
  The real thing, as an Idea in the Kantian sense, transcends both the single appearances and the noematic unity offered in a manifold of them.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-noema-as-phenomenologically-reduced-object` · pp. 77-78 · [The Noema as Phenomenologically Reduced "Object"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-noema-as-phenomenologically-reduced-object)
  > The real thing therefore transcends not only the conscious appearances taken one by one but also the noematic unity intuitively offered in a manifold of them.

- **revised** · `transzendenz/bernet/021` · *transcendence*
  Husserl moves from the natural distinction of immanence and transcendence, through an attempt to reduce transcendence to immanence, to an irreducible difference between the spatial object's transcendence and its immanent modes of givenness.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-noema-as-phenomenologically-reduced-object` · p. 78 · [The Noema as Phenomenologically Reduced "Object"](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-noema-as-phenomenologically-reduced-object)
  > attempts in idealist style to reduce transcendence to immanence, and finds himself forced to extend that immanence to the domain of noematic data, before finally returning to the transcendental-phenomenological finding of an irreducible difference between the transcendence of the spatial object and its immanent noetic-noematic modes of givenness.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/bernet/022` · *transcending*
  By transcending the things of the world, the reduction reveals at one stroke the world as world and the subject as subject.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h3-3-the-world-husserl` · pp. 93-94 · [3. The World (Husserl)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-world-husserl)
  > By transcending the things of the world the reduction reveals at one stroke the world as world and the subject as subject.

- **criticized** · `transzendenz/bernet/023` · *transcendent world*
  The hypothesis of the world's annihilation rests on a Cartesian dualism between immanent consciousness and the transcendent world, which blocks understanding of constitution.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-i` · pp. 97-98 · [I](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#i)
  > It rests on the Cartesian-type ontological dualism between the evident being of immanent consciousness and the dubitable being of the transcendent world, a dualism that at bottom obstructs any understanding of what transcendental constitution of the world by the subject means.

- **introduced** · `transzendenz/bernet/024` · *transcendence*
  Intramundane comportments are doubly constituting: their intentionality carries them toward things and persons, and their transcendence reveals and shapes the world.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-i` · pp. 103-104 · [I](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#i)
  > Intramundane comportments are thus doubly constituting: their intentionality carries them toward things and persons, and their transcendence reveals and shapes the world.

  Because the surrounding world transcends everything in it, it can manifest itself only to a subject capable of transcending its commerce with intramundane beings, as in birth and death.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-ii` · pp. 106-107 · [II](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#ii)

  > For Husserl the surrounding world and the universal world reveal themselves as forms of transcendence exceeding one's being-in-the-world, from which one nonetheless receives the full understanding of one's existence-in-the-world

  > The revelation of the world depends on a subject transcending its immediate environment and its being-in-the-world

  > Husserl's notion of constitution does not permit the full measure of the world's transcendence to be taken

  Rather than revealing itself as the work of human beings, the world reveals to them the finitude of their transcendence.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-iii` · pp. 117-118 · [III](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#iii)
